chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Riab, from Abi Ubayda al-Hadhdha, from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Whoever gives fatwa to the people without knowledge or true guidance, the angels of mercy and the angels of punishment curse him, and the burden of the one who acts by his fatwa attaches to him.
ai.seo_question: What are the consequences of giving fatwa without knowledge in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith outlines the legal and spiritual consequences for those who issue religious rulings (fatwa) without sufficient knowledge and guidance. It states that such individuals are cursed by both the angels of mercy and the angels of punishment, and they bear the weight of the deeds of those who follow their rulings.

en.ammaar-muslim: 1. [1/-] al-Kafi: Muhammad b. Yahya from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Isa from al-Hasan b. Mahbub from Ali b. Riab from Abi Ubayda al-Hadhdha from Abi Ja’far عليه السلام who said:

whoever gives Fatwa to the people without knowledge or true guidance the angels of mercy do curse him and so do too the angels of punishment and the burden of the one who acts by his Fatwa attaches itself to him.
